close_reason:
Added TimeZone and TimeZoneRule typed sub-types to jmap-jscalendar-types per RFC 8984 §4.7.2. Deviation from bead description: the spec defines a single TimeZoneRule used in BOTH standard[] and daylight[] array slots, not separate StandardTimeZoneRule/DaylightTimeZoneRule. Implementation follows the spec.

Changes:
- crate-jmap-jscalendar-types/src/lib.rs: added TimeZone (8 fields) and TimeZoneRule (7 fields) with #[non_exhaustive], @type discriminator, camelCase, extras field. PatchObject imported from jmap_types for recurrenceOverrides.
- 4 new tests: 2 extras-preservation + 1 STANDARD-rule round-trip mirroring RFC 8984 §4.7.2 Europe/Berlin shape + 1 recurrenceOverrides empty-patch invariant.
- Re-exported from jmap-tasks-types and jmap-calendars-types lib.rs.
- Upgraded Task.time_zones test (tasks-types) from Value-only to typed: deserialize Task, extract per-entry Value, decode to TimeZone, assert wire shape preserved.
- Added new CalendarEvent.time_zones typed-decode test (calendars-types).
- PLAN.md updates: jscalendar-types Object types table, tasks-types and calendars-types timezone field annotations.

Gates clean: cargo test --workspace (113 'ok' lines, 0 failed), cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p jmap-jscalendar-types --no-deps.
description:
RFC 8984 §4.7.2 `timeZones` is `Map<TimeZoneId, TimeZone>` where TimeZone is a JSCalendar object (id, names, standard/daylight offsets, transitions, etc.). `jmap-jscalendar-types` does NOT currently model the TimeZone type — only a String reference (e.g. `Location.time_zone: Option<String>` which is a tz-identifier reference, not a full TimeZone object).

This means `Task.time_zones` (sloppy Value field in jmap-tasks-types) and the equivalent `CalendarEvent.time_zones` (jmap-calendars-types) cannot be type-decoded via `jmap_jscalendar_types::TimeZone` — the type does not exist.

Discovered while implementing JMAP-yfpq.2 (round-trip tests for tasks sloppy-Value fields). Test for `time_zones` had to fall back to a Value-only round-trip with no typed assertion.

Scope options:
  A. Add `pub struct TimeZone { id, ... names, ... standard, daylight }` plus dependent types (StandardTimeZoneRule, DaylightTimeZoneRule per RFC 8984 §4.7.2). This is a moderate-size addition: TimeZone has ~10 fields and references LocalDateTime + new Rule structs with byday/bymonth recurrence fragments.
  B. Accept the gap permanently. `time_zones` is one of the more obscure JSCalendar fields and most consumers will never touch it directly. The sloppy Value round-trips fine on the wire; typed access just isn't available.
  C. Add only TimeZone (no rule types), modelling standard/daylight as serde_json::Value. Half-measure.

Recommendation: A — fully type it. Matches the pattern of every other sub-type in jmap-jscalendar-types being fully typed, and removes the asymmetry where Task.time_zones is the only one of the 11 sloppy fields without a typed counterpart.

Acceptance:
- TimeZone, StandardTimeZoneRule, DaylightTimeZoneRule structs added per RFC 8984 §4.7.2.
- All #[non_exhaustive], all camelCase, all with @type wire tags per workspace convention.
- Re-exported from jmap-jscalendar-types lib.rs.
- Re-exported from jmap-tasks-types lib.rs (and jmap-calendars-types) for symmetry.
- Round-trip test for Task.time_zones in jmap-tasks-types is upgraded from Value-only to typed.
- Round-trip test for CalendarEvent.time_zones in jmap-calendars-types follows the same upgrade.

Not blocking JMAP-yfpq.2 — that bead can close with 10 typed tests + 1 Value-only test for time_zones.
title: jmap-jscalendar-types: TimeZone sub-type missing — Task.time_zones cannot be typed-decoded
